clue.text: Refuse to see most of Irish county

indicators.note: most of says the county's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Offaly is a county in the Irish midlands

explanation.surface: Someone declines to visit the bulk of a county in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning waste; 'most of' drops the Y from OFFALY. 'to see' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the waste parts of a butchered animal, so it is literally refuse.

clue.text: Crossed high above flood before noon

parts.note: to overflow is to flood

explanation.surface: Something soared over a flood just before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft passing far above territory has travelled across it in the air.

clue.text: Religious song turned into French

indicators.note: into places the reversed tune within the abbreviation for French
turned means the word for song is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A sacred hymn was translated into French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' looks like an adjective, but as a noun it means a member of a religious order; 'turned' signals the reversal and 'into' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order, and 'religious' as a noun means such a person.

clue.text: How beastly the Pope once was!

definitions.text: How beastly the Pope once was!

parts.words: How beastly the Pope once was!
parts.note: beastly read as like a big cat, and the Pope as one of the popes called Leo

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how awful a former pontiff was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like 'nasty', but means like a lion; the adjective also describes things of Pope Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lionlike and also relates to one of the popes named Leo.

clue.text: One may give camper aid when injured

definitions.text: One may give camper aid when injured

indicators.note: injured suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who might help a hurt holidaymaker in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and 'when injured' rearranges CAMPER AID.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance medic is exactly the person who treats a hurt camper.

clue.text: Easily led to include one in equipment

indicators.note: to include means the word for equipment takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: plant is industrial machinery or equipment
I, the Roman numeral, means one

explanation.surface: Someone easily persuaded to bring one along in their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliant person is compliant and readily influenced.

clue.text: Extremely rude casual worker given tranquilliser

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the extremes of the next word

parts.note: lax means casual or slack
an ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A very coarse temporary employee is handed a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'rude', but it takes R and E, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaxant is a drug that calms or loosens muscles, as a sedative does.

clue.text: Officer's order

definitions.meaning: to arrange or set in order

explanation.surface: An instruction issued by an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a senior officer, and to marshal troops is to arrange them in order.

clue.text: I condemn a corrupt authority

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denounces a crooked power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' looks like an adjective for 'authority', but it rearranges I CONDEMN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is control or power over others.

clue.text: Chopped spice

definitions.meaning: past tense of cleave, to split with a blade
a dried flower bud used in cooking

explanation.surface: A seasoning that has been cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Clove is a past tense of cleave, to split; cloves are also an aromatic spice.

clue.text: Express view, for example, in this

definitions.text: Express view, for example, in this

parts.words: Express view, for example, in this
parts.note: the Express is a British daily paper, and its view is set out in a particular column

explanation.surface: Where a newspaper airs its opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb, but it is the Daily Express newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article states the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Capital none preferred to Paris

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
O, zero, means none

explanation.surface: Some capital city is ranked above Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris here is not the city but Juliet's other suitor in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Romeo and Juliet, Juliet loves the Montague youth rather than the County Paris her parents favour.

clue.text: Currency dealings for au pair?

definitions.meaning: a young foreigner taken into a household in return for help, a swap of sorts

explanation.surface: Money trading done on behalf of a live-in helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading money between currencies is a financial market term; an au pair is a person from abroad in an exchange arrangement.

clue.text: There was a mountain of this fruit

definitions.text: There was a mountain of this fruit

parts.words: There was a mountain of this fruit
parts.note: a hill near Jerusalem in the Bible is named after this small oily fruit

explanation.surface: A glut of some fruit once piled up high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mountain of' suggests a surplus, but it means the Mount near Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mount of Olives is the biblical hill east of Jerusalem, and the fruit is from the tree it names.

clue.text: In extremes of terror, I endlessly imagine plots

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremes of asks for the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for imagine loses its final letter

parts.note: to guess is to imagine or suppose

explanation.surface: In utter fear, someone keeps dreaming up schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of terror' gives TR; 'endlessly' trims GUESS to GUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigues are secret schemes, the same as plots.

clue.text: Soulful witticism?

parts.note: read as a ship carrying just a single soul, and also a short joke

explanation.surface: A deeply felt quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soulful' is read as 'with one soul aboard', a single-passenger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick quip in a single sentence; also, jokingly, a ship holding a sole person.

clue.text: Start off period in government in official abode

indicators.note: start off means the first letter of the term of office is removed

parts.note: a presidency is a president's period in office

explanation.surface: Someone begins a term of office in an official home.
explanation.definitionFit: A residency is an official residence, such as an envoy's.

clue.text: Showing contempt, that is, over an article

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the abbreviation above what follows

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means that is
A means an
a thing is an article or object

explanation.surface: Contempt shown, that is, about some article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like a link, but gives SC, from scilicet; 'an article' gives A THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing remarks are harshly critical and scornful.

clue.text: Bird starts to nest under roof

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of the two following words

parts.note: thatch is a roof of straw or reeds

explanation.surface: A bird begins nesting beneath a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small European tree-climbing songbird.

clue.text: Messenger or porter carrying letters

indicators.note: carrying means the beer word holds the mail word inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
post is mail, letters

explanation.surface: A courier or doorman delivering mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a carrier of bags, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is literally one sent out, a messenger of a faith.

clue.text: A British queen once as community leader

parts.note: Bess was the familiar name for Elizabeth I, a former queen

explanation.surface: A former British queen serves as a local figurehead.
explanation.walkthrough: The community is a religious one, a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the head of a community of nuns.

clue.text: Nobleman losing ring in London borough

indicators.note: in places the ring shape inside the borough's name

parts.note: Barnet is a borough of north London
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A titled man loses a ring in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Nobleman, losing ring, (is) in London borough': take O from the nobleman and BARNET, a north London borough, remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking below a baron.

clue.text: Not so bad. I'll wager

definitions.meaning: a person who wagers money, a punter

explanation.surface: A gambler says things are improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Better is the comparative of good, and a better is one who bets.

clue.text: Not easy to find fine, in practical circumstances

parts.note: fine, as in fine thread, means thin
on the ground means in the real working situation, not in theory

explanation.surface: Something is scarce, rather than fine, in real-world conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like praise, but it means thin and slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce or sparse is hard to come by.

clue.text: Sum for workers limited by cap

indicators.note: limited by means the workers are enclosed within the word for cap

parts.note: a top is a cap or lid
TU, trade union, is a body of workers

explanation.surface: An amount for staff is capped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cap' looks like a limit, but it is a top or lid.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to add them together.

clue.text: Federation heading off trouble that's afoot

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: A league prevents trouble that is brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' looks like 'under way', but means on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is an alliance or federation of states.

clue.text: Where one's money may be soundly tied up?

indicators.note: soundly says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: trussed means tied up, as a chicken for roasting

explanation.surface: Asking where savings might be safely locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'securely', but it signals a homophone of TRUSSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Money can be held in a trust, a legal arrangement managed for beneficiaries.

clue.text: Temporarily accommodated by one on purpose

parts.note: staying in a tent is a temporary lodging
I, the Roman numeral, means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was put up for a while by another person deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temporarily accommodated' gives IN TENT; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal is what one intends.

clue.text: Rider not effectively adding anything

definitions.meaning: one who travels in a vehicle without driving it
a team member who contributes nothing and is carried by the others

explanation.surface: A rider who contributes nothing useful.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in a car or bus is carried along; so is a team member who does no work.

clue.text: Make name in very restricted environment? Aussie can

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name inside the word for a cramped space

parts.note: a very small space is tiny

explanation.surface: Becoming famous in a cramped setting, an Australian manages it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is link; 'can' looks like a verb but is a beer can.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a tinny is a can of beer.
